Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Every morphism of the
framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]] is a finite composite of tensor
products of identities, crossings, cups, caps and full twists.

A complete presentation on this elementary family is Turaev's reduced
presentation (3.1.a), (3.2.a)--(3.2.h), **together with** the expressions
(2.5.d)--(2.5.e) and (3.1.b)--(3.1.c) defining its additional orientation
variants. Thus two elementary words represent the same framed tangle exactly
when these relations and the strict monoidal axioms relate them.

Here the source's $X^\delta$ denotes our $X^\delta_{+,+}$, its
$Z^\delta$ denotes our $X^{-\delta}_{+,-}$, and its $Y^\delta$ denotes our
$X^{-\delta}_{-,+}$; its $T^\delta$ denotes our $X^\delta_{-,-}$.
The source's positive cup and cap are $\cup_+$ and $\cap_+$, and its
$\varphi,\varphi'$ are $\varphi_+^+,\varphi_+^-$.
The reduced generators are therefore $X^\delta_{+,+}$,
$X^{-\delta}_{+,-}$, $\varphi_+^{\pm1}$, $\cup_+$ and $\cap_+$.
The other cups, caps and crossings are the expressions above; a twist on a
negative strand is obtained by bending the corresponding twisted positive
strand with a cup and cap. Turaev's convention that a positive strand points
downwards is transported to ours by reversing all strand orientations; this
preserves composition, tensor product and framed isotopy. Crossing
superscripts in his mixed-orientation pictures are oriented signs, explaining
the minus signs in the dictionary.

The reduced relations are Yang--Baxter, the two zig-zags, inverse crossings
and twists, curl slide, the bent-crossing inverse relation (3.2.g), and the
twist-square relation (3.2.h). For example, the latter has the well-typed form

$$(\varphi_+^+)^2=(\cap_+\otimes1_+)(1_-\otimes X^+_{+,+})(X^-_{+,-}\otimes1_+)(\cup_+\otimes1_+).$$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

These are the right coevaluation and evaluation on $X$ induced by the ribbon
structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

Let $(\mathcal C,c)$ be a braided monoidal category. Then there exists a strict
monoidal category $\mathcal D$, a braiding $c^{\mathrm{str}}$ on $\mathcal D$,
and a monoidal equivalence $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ such that $F$ is a
braided monoidal functor.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Work first in [F4]'s strict model. Write $b_Y:\mathbf1\to Y\otimes Y^*$, $e_Y:Y^*\otimes Y\to\mathbf1$, $r_Y=e_{Y^*}(j_Y\otimes1)$ and $b_Y^R=(1\otimes j_Y^{-1})b_{Y^*}$. Assign the listed generator values and each coupon its morphism. Slice any generic diagram between all crossings, extrema, recorded twists and coupon levels, then evaluate by categorical tensor product/composition. The strand-only equations of [F1] hold with arbitrary branch colors: Yang–Baxter follows by the naturality/hexagon expansion on $U,V,W$; each inverse and snake has its own actual color; the bent-crossing equation is the arbitrary-$V,W$ composite in [F2]; its inverse-order proof and opposite braiding give all signs; and the twist-square computation of [F2] applies to each arbitrary single $Y$. Redundant orientation variants are its right-dual composites applied separately to each color. Thus no equality of unequal objects or single-color specialization is used to justify multicolored relations.

For $f:|A|\to|B|$, the two displayed crossing/coupon equations are exactly naturality of $c$; multiplying by its inverses gives both underpass versions. Expanding each tensor-list crossing by the two hexagons writes the actual finite word of crossings of one band with all inputs/outputs of the coupon. Upward bands are their dual tensor objects and use the already checked bent-crossing formulas, so these equations cover every orientation. For full rotations define $\Theta_\varnothing=1$ and $\Theta_{A\otimes Y}=c_{Y,A}c_{A,Y}(\Theta_A\otimes\theta_Y)$. Balancing inductively gives $\Theta_A=\theta_{|A|}$, including all individual twists and all pairwise full-bunch crossings. Naturality gives $\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f$, exactly the input-bunch inverse/output-bunch full rotation, with no deleted framing twist.

For $f:A\otimes Y\to B$ define its typed left mate $f^\flat=(f\otimes1_{Y^*})(1_A\otimes b_Y):A\to B\otimes Y^*$. The inverse is $(1_B\otimes e_Y)(f^\flat\otimes1_Y)$. Substitution and the two snakes show both composites are identities on these Hom spaces. The other bends use $b_Y^R,r_Y$ and their two snakes. Iteration supplies every signed-list orientation and the needed double-dual comparison $j$; two full dualizations are consistent because $j_Bf=f^{**}j_A$. Coupon composition/tensor rules are the actual equalities $gf$ and $f\otimes g$. Thus all evaluations of bent or subdivided coupons have explicitly inverse composites, with no unnamed duality scalar.

To prove that these equations suffice geometrically, take a boundary-relative graph isotopy and choose disjoint solid rectangular neighborhoods of its finitely many coupons, carried along their tracks. Compactness and finite time subdivision permit smaller such moving neighborhoods disjoint from all other bands except their incident fixed collars. Any homotopy of their frame motions is realized by an ambient isotopy there: prescribe its velocity on each rectangle, multiply by a smooth cutoff in its disjoint moving neighborhood and integrate the resulting time-dependent vector field. Its flow fixes the external collars and carries the incident band collars. Time subdivision keeps these supports disjoint. This reduces frame control to finitely many paths in $SO(3)$ with fixed endpoint frames.

Every resulting rotation loop can be homotoped relative endpoints to planar rotations. Explicitly, unit quaternions form $S^3$ and $q:v\mapsto qvq^{-1}$ gives a locally invertible two-sheeted map onto $SO(3)$ with kernel $\{\pm1\}$. A smooth loop in $S^3$ misses a point after a small perturbation and contracts by stereographic projection to $\mathbb R^3$, so $S^3$ is simply connected. Hence an $SO(3)$ loop is classified by whether its lift ends at $+1$ or$-1$. A planar $2\pi$ rotation lifts from $+1$ to$-1$, so planar rotations realize both classes. The cutoff extension of step 2.3 realizes the homotopies on the graph. It follows that the isotopy reduces to motions keeping coupons parallel to the projection plane with horizontal based edges, together with finitely many planar $\pm2\pi$ coupon rotations. The latter are the complete twist relation of step 2.1.

For the remaining motions protect smaller coupon rectangles and keep their incident band collars fixed. Apply [F1]'s generic movie construction to the exterior core arcs, with its perturbation cutoffs vanishing in those collars. Away from coupons its event list is unchanged. At a protected rectangle there are also generic isolated edge tangencies and corner passages; they are retained, not excluded by a false codimension count. In a small disk a smooth-edge tangency has the form $y=u^2+s$ against the edge $y=0$, possibly with both signs reversed. The spatial strand is strictly above or strictly below the coupon in that disk, since the actual graph is embedded; compactness gives a fixed nonzero height separation there. Attachments lie strictly inside the coupon bases, so the disk may be chosen disjoint from every attachment collar. A corner passage is a strand crossing the two-edge junction transversely; its local resolution is given below. Multiple simultaneous events and higher-order edge contacts add a condition to these already retained normal forms, and only those higher degeneracies are excluded by independent jets.

Resolve an edge tangency as follows. Shrink the coupon a little inside its protected neighborhood, replacing each moved attachment by a short parallel identity strip; this changes neither its color nor its input/output tensor order. The same spatial height separation keeps the external strand disjoint throughout. The small U-shaped strand segment $y=u^2+s$ now gives two successive entries/exits past the shrunken edge. Separate them in slicing height and bend its turn by the explicit mate bijection of step 2.2. Each straight passage is a naturality equation from step 2.1 or its inverse. When only part of the short based strips lies in that small disk, enlarge the local word by inserting the missing crossings paired immediately with their inverses outside the coupon. In algebraic terms the full naturality word is $C_B(f\otimes1)=(1\otimes f)C_A$, where $C_A=c_{|A|,Z}$ and $C_B=c_{|B|,Z}$, or its other-side/inverse version. The completed event is this exact equation pre/post-composed with the same exterior words $L,R$; expand $C_A,C_B$ by the hexagon to match the actual based-strip order. Removing the adjacent inserted inverse pairs recovers the two original readings of the event. No cancellation is moved through $f$, and no naturality for a partial input subobject of $f$ is asserted: the missing input and output crossing words can differ. For the two consecutive passages of the U segment, complete both together, so their exterior words on each fixed side are inverse. Those words reduce to $C_A^{-1}C_A=1$ on the input side and $C_BC_B^{-1}=1$ on the output side, with their respective actual tensor types. Retract the auxiliary bend by its snake. Thus the entire edge-tangency event changes no evaluated morphism. The negative quadratic contact reverses this derivation. A cap instead of a cup uses the inverse mate, an upward strand uses $Z^*$, and an underpass uses the inverse-crossing naturality, all explicitly established in step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2. This covers both orientations, over/under choices, both edge sides and both contact signs. The local shrink only alters attachment-free portions of the protected rectangle, so a base-edge event is treated exactly like a side-edge event; short based strips are included in the sublist completion just described.

For a corner passage choose a disk containing that corner but no attachments. Round or cut off the corner of the protected coupon inside that disk, joining the unchanged two based-edge portions by a smooth arc. This is a planar isotopy of an attachment-free part of the coupon and changes no morphism or tensor list. The external strand stays spatially separated above/below it. Perturb the rounded arc slightly so the corner passage is replaced by two ordinary edge passages and, if the strand turns back in that disk, one quadratic edge tangency. The two possible routes around the old corner differ by the consecutive passage and its inverse; their expanded words cancel as in step 5.1. Thus restoring the corner yields the same value. The four corners differ only in which edge is a base edge; all attachments remain outside the disk, so step 5.1's sublist completion applies to each. This supplies the corner events instead of excluding their generic isolated times.

A coupon level may cross an exterior extremum level or a crossing level at an isolated time; these slicing events are also retained. If their support disks are disjoint from the protected rectangle, their generator words exchange by interchange. If adjacent in projection, shrink the rectangle as in step 5.1 so the extremum/crossing lies outside it. The induced strand passages are the partial/full naturality words already resolved there; a cup or cap adjacent to the coupon is handled by step 2.2's mate bijection and its inverse snake, and a crossing of its short incident strips is moved by [F1]'s cup passage or third move before the naturality word. Moving the coupon back cancels the inserted inverse words. Thus neither a slicing extremum nor a crossing-level event is silently removed from the movie. If two projected coupon rectangles pass each other, shrink one and move its short incident strips past the other successively, then exchange their disjoint levels. The complete identity is $c_{|B|,|D|}(f\otimes g)=(g\otimes f)c_{|A|,|C|}$, obtained by the two naturality equations successively; edge/corner events during this shrink were handled in step 5.1, step 6.1. This covers all valences and the empty tensor list. The retained event list is exhaustive because every remaining regular projected arc/coupon incidence is transverse, every nonregular one has precisely one of the stated edge/corner normal forms after the generic perturbation, and all exterior core singularities and framing events are [F1]'s list.

There are finitely many events by [F1]'s compactness/relative genericity argument applied to this finite graph with its protected rectangle collars. Every event preserves the composite by step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1; between them only slicing levels and disjoint-factor interchange change. The whole framed isotopy therefore preserves evaluation. The generator assignment preserves composition/tensor products and the empty diagram by definition; every diagram has the sliced form, so it also proves uniqueness. Transport through [F4]'s strong monoidal equivalence gives the claimed evaluation in the original category, with all chosen dual comparisons inserted as in [F2]. Only [A1]'s inherited countable choice is used; all additional neighborhoods, frame adjustments and word operations are finite.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals. Consider finite oriented framed ribbon graphs with boundary collars, bands colored by arbitrary objects of $\mathcal C$, and coupons colored by arbitrary morphisms between the tensor products of their incident signed objects. There is a unique monoidal evaluation assigning each coupon its declared morphism, crossings the braiding or its correctly typed inverse, cups/caps the chosen duality maps and their ribbon-induced opposite variants, and full twists $\theta^{\pm1}$. It is invariant under every boundary-relative framed graph isotopy and preserves composition, tensor product and the empty graph. In a strict model it is strict monoidal; transport gives the corresponding strong monoidal evaluation in $\mathcal C$.

More precisely, for a signed list $A=(Y_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,Y_p^{\epsilon_p})$, put $|A|=\bigotimes_sY_s^{\epsilon_s}$, with $Y^-=Y^*$. For a coupon $f:|A|\to|B|$, its strand passages and full rotation are the complete composites

$$c_{|B|,Z}(f\otimes1_Z)=(1_Z\otimes f)c_{|A|,Z},\qquad c_{Z,|B|}(1_Z\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_Z)c_{Z,|A|},\qquad\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f.$$

Their tensor-list expansions, all inverse-crossing versions and the explicit dual-mate formulas supply every coupon move; the claim includes zero-input/output coupons and all band orientations. No assumption that all colors are tensor powers of one object is imposed.

A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.
For every simple object $i$ of a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit and pivotal map $j$, its pivotal dimension $d_i=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_i)$ is nonzero.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a spherical tensor category over an algebraically closed field $k$, with spherical structure $a$.
For every object $X$ and every endomorphism $x:X\to X$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(a_Xx)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(xa_X^{-1}).$$

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: For each $X$ choose actual $u_{i,a}:i\to X$, $v^{i,a}:X\to i$ with $v^{i,a}u_{j,b}=\delta_{ij}\delta_{ab}1_i$ and $\sum_{i,a}u_{i,a}v^{i,a}=1_X$. Define $\iota_X=\sum_{i,a}\iota_i(u_{i,a}^*\otimes v^{i,a}):X^*\otimes X\to B$. Changing a multiplicity-space basis multiplies the two entries by inverse matrices, leaving this sum unchanged. For $f:X\to Y$, expand its scalar simple blocks $v_Yfu_X$ in the two decompositions. This gives the exact dinaturality equation $\iota_Y(1_{Y^*}\otimes f)=\iota_X(f^*\otimes1_X)$. If another family $t_X:X^*\otimes X\to Z$ obeys that equation, its finite decomposition is $t_X=\sum_{i,a}t_i(u_{i,a}^*\otimes v^{i,a})$. Thus the unique map $t:B\to Z$ with $t\iota_i=t_i$ satisfies $t\iota_X=t_X$. This proves the coend property explicitly, including uniqueness, without an existence or Fubini theorem.

Define the required structural maps by $\Delta\iota_X=(\iota_X\otimes\iota_X)(1_{X^*}\otimes b_X\otimes1_X)$, $\varepsilon\iota_X=e_X$, and $m(\iota_X\otimes\iota_Y)=\iota_{Y\otimes X}(1_{X^*}\otimes c_{X,Y^*\otimes Y})$. The last target uses $(Y\otimes X)^*=X^*\otimes Y^*$, or its canonical dual comparison. These formulas define maps first on the finitely many simple summands. Dinaturality, braiding naturality and the explicit dual-mate identities in [F1] show that their stated words hold for arbitrary $X,Y$, proving well-definedness under every choice of decomposition. Substituting the first two words gives $(1_B\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta\iota_X=(\iota_X\otimes e_X)(1_{X^*}\otimes b_X\otimes1_X)=\iota_X$ by a snake; the opposite snake gives $(\varepsilon\otimes1_B)\Delta=1_B$ too. No other Hopf algebra axiom is needed.

Fix simple $j,k$ and decompose each $i\otimes j$ using $u_{k,a}:k\to i\otimes j$ and $v^{k,a}:i\otimes j\to k$, with $v^{k,b}u_{k,a}=\delta_{ab}1_k$. Set $F_{i,a}=(v^{k,a}\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes b_j):i\to k\otimes j^*$ and $G_{i,a}=(1_i\otimes r_j)(u_{k,a}\otimes1_{j^*}):k\otimes j^*\to i$. Their inverses as adjunction correspondences insert $e_j$ or $b_j^R$ and retract a snake, so the $F$ and $G$ families span the respective simple multiplicity spaces. Define $\operatorname{ptr}_j(a)=(1_i\otimes r_j)(a\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes b_j)$ on $a\in\operatorname{End}(i\otimes j)$. The displayed words give $G_{i,b}F_{i,a}=\operatorname{ptr}_j(u_{k,b}v^{k,a})$. Closing in stages and then cyclically gives $\operatorname{tr}_i(G_{i,b}F_{i,a})=\operatorname{tr}_{i\otimes j}(u_{k,b}v^{k,a})=\operatorname{tr}_k(v^{k,a}u_{k,b})=\delta_{ab}d_k$. Since $i$ is simple, $G_{i,b}F_{i,a}=\delta_{ab}(d_k/d_i)1_i$; compositions with different simple labels vanish. Consequently the actual complete trace-dual resolution on $k\otimes j^*$ is $\sum_{i,a}d_iF_{i,a}G_{i,a}=d_k1_{k\otimes j^*}$. This includes every fusion multiplicity and uses no positivity.

For the two-$\Omega$ slide, cut its participating components near the attaching band and place those endpoint pairs adjacently below the remaining graph. Evaluating that exterior with variable cut colors gives $T_{X,Y}:X^*\otimes X\otimes Y^*\otimes Y\otimes U\to V$, retaining arbitrary other boundary factors and coupons. It is dinatural in the two surgery variables: a morphism inserted on their paths passes crossings by [F1]'s naturality, twists by twist naturality and bends by its explicit inverse mate formulas; no coupon lies on a surgery component itself. Define $\Phi:B\otimes B\otimes U\to V$ by its simple restrictions $\Phi(\iota_i\otimes\iota_j\otimes1_U)=T_{i,j}$. step 1.1's finite decomposition proves $T_{X,Y}=\Phi(\iota_X\otimes\iota_Y\otimes1_U)$ for all $X,Y$. This is the full exterior factorization, including arbitrary external coupons, not a claim that those coupons are natural as functions of their own graph colors.

For $a\in\operatorname{End}(k\otimes j^*)$ define the literal composite $T_{kj}(a)=(1_{k^*}\otimes1_k\otimes e_j)(1_{k^*}\otimes a\otimes1_j)(b_k^R\otimes1_{j^*}\otimes1_j):j^*\otimes j\to k^*\otimes k$. It sends the identity to $b_k^Re_j$. Substituting $F,G$ gives $T_{kj}(F_{i,a}G_{i,a})=(u_{k,a}^*\otimes v^{k,a})(1_{j^*}\otimes b_i^R\otimes1_j)$. To check every bend, first expand $F$: its $b_j$ and the final $e_j$ retract by the $j^*$ snake, leaving $v^{k,a}$ on $i\otimes j$. In the other half use $(1_{k^*}\otimes u_{k,a})b_k^R=(u_{k,a}^*\otimes1_{i\otimes j})b_{i\otimes j}^R$, the dual-mate coevaluation identity. Expand $b_{i\otimes j}^R=(1_{j^*}\otimes b_i^R\otimes1_j)b_j^R$; the $r_j$ in $G$ retracts the outer right snake. The remaining word is exactly the stated $u^*,b_i^R,v$ composite, with domain $j^*\otimes j$ and target $k^*\otimes k$. Applying $T$ to step 2.2's resolution thus proves the complete morphism identity $\sum_{i,a}d_i(u_{k,a}^*\otimes v^{k,a})(1_{j^*}\otimes b_i^R\otimes1_j)=d_kb_k^Re_j$.

Put $\Lambda=\sum_i d_i\iota_ib_i^R$. Braiding naturality at $b_i^R$ says $c_{j,i^*\otimes i}(1_j\otimes b_i^R)=b_i^R\otimes1_j$. Hence the multiplication word gives $m(\iota_j\otimes\Lambda)=\sum_i d_i\iota_{i\otimes j}(1_{j^*}\otimes b_i^R\otimes1_j)$. Expand $\iota_{i\otimes j}$ using step 1.1 and apply step 3.1 separately for each output $k$. The result is $\sum_k d_k\iota_kb_k^Re_j=\Lambda e_j$. The $\iota_j$ are all summand inclusions, so this is the full identity $m(1_B\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\varepsilon$. step 2.1 consequently gives $\Gamma(1_B\otimes\Lambda)=(1_B\otimes\Lambda\varepsilon)\Delta=1_B\otimes\Lambda$, and precomposing with $\Lambda$ gives $\Gamma(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\otimes\Lambda$. This is a full-channel calculation and does not use a simple-meridian projector, modular inversion, Gauss sums or surgery normalization.

Inserting $\Lambda$ at a component cut is exactly the finite formal coloring $\Omega$: $b_i^R$ closes its two oriented cut endpoints and its coefficient is $d_i$. Reversing that component's orientation replaces $i$ by $i^*$; dual-mate compatibility of $j$, ribbon twist duality, and sphericality $d_i=d_{i^*}$ give the same evaluated graph after reindexing the sum. Thus no independent antipode or integral theorem is needed for orientation reversal. Moving a pair of $\Lambda$ cuts past each other also does not change their value, since naturality gives $c_{B,B}(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\otimes\Lambda$ from $c_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}=1$.

The complete endpoint word created by the framed band sum on those two cuts is $(\iota_X\otimes\iota_{Y\otimes X})(1_{X^*}\otimes1_X\otimes1_{X^*}\otimes c_{X,Y^*\otimes Y})(1_{X^*}\otimes b_X\otimes1_X\otimes1_{Y^*}\otimes1_Y)$, exactly $\Gamma(\iota_X\otimes\iota_Y)$. To read it geometrically, follow the rectangle of the attaching band: the slid strand turns around one end, making $b_X$ and its $X^*$ return; its new parallel follows the stationary strand in its specified framing; at the other end $X$ passes the ordered pair $Y^*,Y$, giving $c_{X,Y^*\otimes Y}$ with its hexagon expansion. The two parallels have cable color $Y\otimes X$ and reversed dual cable $X^*\otimes Y^*$. The new parallel follows the entire stationary component outside the little band ball: applying the same exterior $\Phi$ to $\iota_{Y\otimes X}$ accounts for that whole cable. Every exterior crossing cables by the hexagons and every exterior twist by balancing. Thus no false assertion that the global band sum is supported in the attaching-band ball is made. Its full evaluation is $\Phi(\Gamma(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)\otimes1_U)$, equal to $\Phi(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda\otimes1_U)$ by step 4.1. The rectangle's framing is retained: any twist in it or in the stationary parallel is read on both sides by the same cable twist word, never discarded by an unframed move.

For an open strand keep its fixed color $Y$ and its entire factor $Y^*\otimes Y$, rather than imposing coend dinaturality in a coupon-dependent graph variable. The displayed operator $\widehat\Gamma_Y$ first sends $Y^*\otimes Y$ to $(Y^*\otimes Y)\otimes(Y^*\otimes Y)$ by $1_{Y^*}\otimes b_Y\otimes1_Y$, then sends only the second pair through $\iota_Y$ before multiplication with the surgery variable. step 4.1 implies $m(\iota_Y\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda e_Y$, by step 1.1's finite decomposition if $Y$ is not simple. Substitution into this exact lifted word gives $\widehat\Gamma_Y(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda)=(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda e_Y)(1_{Y^*}\otimes b_Y\otimes1_Y)=1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda$ by the left snake. For simple $j$ the same identity also follows by applying the actual projection $B\to j^*\otimes j$ to $\Gamma(\iota_j\otimes\Lambda)=\iota_j\otimes\Lambda$. Hence it is an identity on the complete open-color factor, not only after a categorical trace.

Fix the actual colored graph and its coupons, and cut only a short interior segment of the strand to be slid. After bending that segment the exterior has type $(Y^*\otimes Y)\otimes B\otimes U\to V$. Its factorization through $B$ uses dinaturality only along the $\Omega$ surgery component, exactly as in step 2.3; the first object $Y$ and every graph coupon remain fixed. The band reading of step 5.2 now uses $\widehat\Gamma_Y$ on that fixed first factor, so step 5.3 equates its before/after composites with the entire fixed exterior. To make the finite-cut method fully explicit, write $1_Y=\sum_{j,a}u_{j,a}v^{j,a}$ and insert that resolution on the short segment before bending. On each term absorb the actual $u_{j,a},v^{j,a}$ into its two adjacent exterior graph portions. Its local segment is now the fixed simple $j$ and step 5.3 applies to that term with those very coupons held constant. Summing restores exactly the original graph; basis independence is the matrix identity $\sum u v=1_Y$. No family of arbitrary coupons indexed by variable $X$ is moved through a universal dinaturality argument.

The bending used in step 6.1 is injective on the relevant open-graph Hom space: for $f:A\otimes Y\to C$, its mate is $(f\otimes1_{Y^*})(1_A\otimes b_Y)$, with inverse $(1_C\otimes e_Y)(-\otimes1_Y)$; their composites are the two snakes. Other incident orientations use $b_Y^R,r_Y$ with their inverse mates. Thus equality of the bent expressions proves equality of the original open-strand morphisms before any closure. If the segment is part of a more complicated coupon-bearing graph, all portions outside its short cut, including junction coupons, are precisely the fixed exterior of step 6.1, so the same equality proves their slide as well. Opposite slide directions read the equality backwards; other orientations and either ordering of the two participating components use step 5.1's explicit dual reindexing and cut interchange. This covers all framed colored-strand and $\Omega$-component cases in the Statement.

All calculations are identities of finite categorical composites, and hence survive arbitrary exterior pre/post-composition and tensor factors. No $D$, Gauss sum, normalized surgery invariant or topological presentation theorem was used. In a surgery application a band slide preserves the component count and changes the linking matrix by $B\mapsto P^tBP$, with $P$ the integral elementary basis change adding the stationary attaching vector to the slid one, so signature is preserved even when singular; that observation adds no assumption to the ribbon identity just proved. Countable choice enters only through [F1]; every fusion basis, cut expansion and coend component sum is finite. The complete local ribbon claims are therefore proved independently of all later Gauss/FR/TQFT consumers.

citations.quote: For every simple object $i$ of a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit and pivotal map $j$, its pivotal dimension $d_i=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_i)$ is nonzero.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular under [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. Let $C$ be the charge-conjugation matrix, $C_{ij}=\delta_{i,j^*}$. Then

$$s^2=D^2C.$$

In particular $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2\ne0$, so either square root $D$ gives an invertible normalized matrix $S=s/D$ with $S^2=C$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be the spherical ribbon fusion category of [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. For simple labels $i,j$,

$$s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_k N_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k,$$

and, for simple labels $x,i,j$,

$$s_{xi}s_{xj}=d_x\sum_kN_{ij}^ks_{xk}.$$

Also $s_{ij}=s_{ji}$, $s_{i^*j^*}=s_{ij}$, $s_{i0}=d_i$, and $d_{i^*}=d_i$. Consequently $h_x(i)=s_{xi}/d_x$ extends linearly to a unital ring character of the fusion ring.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects. Fix a braiding $c$ and a ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism of [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Throughout this pair we use the associated spherical pivotal structure: $j$ is part of the data, and sphericality means $\dim_j(X)=\dim_j(X^\vee)$ for every object, as in [[def-spherical-structure]]. Its trace is $\operatorname{tr}_j(f)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_Xf)$ for $f\in\operatorname{End}(X)$.

Write $0$ for the unit label and $i^*$ for the dual of $i$. Put $N_{ij}^k=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}(k,i\otimes j)$, $d_i=\operatorname{tr}_j(1_i)$, and $s_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}_j(c_{j,i}c_{i,j})$. Define $D^2=\sum_{i\in I}d_i^2$. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix is $s=(s_{ij})$. The ribbon fusion category is **modular** when $s$ is invertible. When $D^2\ne0$, either square root $D$ defines the normalized matrix $S=s/D$; for a modular category, [[lem-modular-hopf-matrix-squared]] proves this nonvanishing. No positivity of the general $d_i$ or of $D$ is assumed.

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals. Consider finite oriented framed ribbon graphs with boundary collars, bands colored by arbitrary objects of $\mathcal C$, and coupons colored by arbitrary morphisms between the tensor products of their incident signed objects. There is a unique monoidal evaluation assigning each coupon its declared morphism, crossings the braiding or its correctly typed inverse, cups/caps the chosen duality maps and their ribbon-induced opposite variants, and full twists $\theta^{\pm1}$. It is invariant under every boundary-relative framed graph isotopy and preserves composition, tensor product and the empty graph. In a strict model it is strict monoidal; transport gives the corresponding strong monoidal evaluation in $\mathcal C$.

More precisely, for a signed list $A=(Y_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,Y_p^{\epsilon_p})$, put $|A|=\bigotimes_sY_s^{\epsilon_s}$, with $Y^-=Y^*$. For a coupon $f:|A|\to|B|$, its strand passages and full rotation are the complete composites

$$c_{|B|,Z}(f\otimes1_Z)=(1_Z\otimes f)c_{|A|,Z},\qquad c_{Z,|B|}(1_Z\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_Z)c_{Z,|A|},\qquad\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f.$$

Their tensor-list expansions, all inverse-crossing versions and the explicit dual-mate formulas supply every coupon move; the claim includes zero-input/output coupons and all band orientations. No assumption that all colors are tensor powers of one object is imposed.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular with $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, and $\kappa=p_+/D$. Then

$$p_+p_-=D^2,\qquad \kappa^{-1}=p_-/D.$$

The formal Kirby color is $\Omega=\sum_i d_i\,i$. A zero-framed $\Omega$ meridian around a simple strand $j$ acts by $D^2\delta_{j,0}$ times the identity, and a $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot evaluates to $p_\pm$. Hence the surgery normalization

$$\tau(M_L)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(L_\Omega)$$

is invariant under adding/removing a disjoint $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot; it gives $\tau(S^3)=D^{-1}$ and $\tau(S^2\times S^1)=1$. The same normalized graph evaluation is invariant under full framed surgery-component handle slides and colored-strand slides over surgery components, with all arbitrary exterior graph coupons retained. A topological theorem asserting completeness of these and relative moves is a separate supplier.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Choose actual finite simple inclusions $u_{k,a}:k\to X$ and projections $v^{k,a}:X\to k$ from a direct sum, with $v^{k,a}u_{l,b}=\delta_{kl}\delta_{ab}1_k$ and $\sum_{k,a}u_{k,a}v^{k,a}=1_X$. Inserting these two identities on either side of any coupon $f:X\to Y$ gives its complete expansion $f=\sum_{k,a,b}u^Y_{k,b}(v_Y^{k,b}fu^X_{k,a})v_X^{k,a}$. Off-diagonal simple terms vanish by Schur's lemma; every remaining middle term is a scalar. Thus this expansion is independent of basis and respects composition/tensor products. Since $\operatorname{tr}_k(v^{k,a}u_{k,b})=d_k\delta_{ab}$, trace-dual projections are $v^{k,a}/d_k$, and the trace-dual resolution is $1_X=\sum_{k,a}d_k u_{k,a}(v^{k,a}/d_k)$. Reversing an edge applies the dual functor and reverses the composite, preserving the identity.

Trace multiplicativity and Frobenius reciprocity give $d_id_j=\sum_kN_{ij}^kd_k$ and $\sum_i d_iN_{ij}^k=d_kd_j$. Summing the balancing expression $s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_kN_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k$ therefore gives $\sum_i\theta_i d_i s_{ij}=p_+\theta_j^{-1}d_j$. Multiply by $s_{j^*,k}$ and sum over $j$. The identity $\sum_js_{ij}s_{j^*,k}=D^2\delta_{ik}$ gives $p_+\sum_j\theta_j^{-1}d_js_{j^*,k}=D^2\theta_kd_k$. At $k=0$, reindexing $j$ by $j^*$ yields $p_+p_-=D^2$. Consequently $p_\pm\ne0$ and $\kappa^{-1}=p_-/D$.

For the unit label, put $x_a=u_{0,a}$, $y_a=v^{0,a}$. Then $y_ax_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $P_X=\sum_a x_ay_a$ is the unit-isotypic projector. It is the identity on $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X)$ and on the opposite dual pairing, because all nonunit components of a map from or to the simple unit vanish. The bending map $f:k\to X\mapsto(f\otimes1)b_k$ has inverse $z\mapsto(1_X\otimes e_k)(z\otimes1_k)$ by the two snakes. Closing a bent pair $f,g$ gives $\operatorname{tr}_k(gf)$, so the same $d_k$ factors of step 1.1 apply after bending.

The displayed partial trace satisfies $\operatorname{ptr}_Z((f\otimes1)a(g\otimes1))=f\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)g$ by interchange. Naturality of both braidings consequently makes each $K_+(X)$ natural in $X$. On simple $j$, step 1.2 gives $K_+(j)=p_+\theta_j^{-1}1_j$. Inserting the full direct-sum resolution gives $K_+(X)=\sum_{j,a}u_{j,a}K_+(j)v^{j,a}=p_+\theta_X^{-1}$ for every object. For the negative version, balancing gives $M_{j,i}^{-1}=(\theta_j\otimes\theta_i)\theta_{j\otimes i}^{-1}$, hence $\operatorname{tr}_jK_-(j)=\sum_{i,k}d_i\theta_i^{-1}\theta_j\theta_iN_{ji}^k\theta_k^{-1}d_k=\theta_jd_jp_-$. Divide by $d_j$ and use the same naturality/resolution to obtain $K_-(X)=p_-\theta_X$.

For arbitrary coupons $a:A\to X$ and $b:X\to B$, step 2.2 says $b\theta_X^{\pm1}K_\pm(X)a=p_\pm ba$. Take $X$ to be the tensor product of every oriented strand through the local surgery annulus, using duals for reversed strands. Repeated hexagons expand $M_{X,i}$ into the full encircling strand word; repeated balancing expands $\theta_X$ into all individual twists and pairwise crossings in its full bunch twist. This explicitly identifies the complete signed twist-surgery composite even if exterior coupons join different members of the bunch. If its eliminated framing is $\epsilon=\pm1$ and linking vector is $\ell$, its matrix $B=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}\epsilon&\ell^t\\\ell&A\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ is congruent to $[\epsilon]\oplus(A-\epsilon\ell\ell^t)$ by replacing each remaining vector $z$ with $z-\epsilon\ell_z u$. Thus $m$ decreases by1 and signature by$\epsilon$. Its graph scalar is $p_\epsilon$, and $D^{-1}\kappa^{-\epsilon}p_\epsilon=1$, proving the normalized signed-move equality with its exact framing/signature factors.

The same naturality makes $E_X$ natural. On simple $j$ its scalar is $d_j^{-1}\sum_i d_i s_{ji}=D^2\delta_{j0}$ by $s^2=D^2C$. Inserting step 1.1 proves $E_X=D^2P_X$ on every object, not just a simple strand. Thus $D^{-2}yE_Xx=yx$ for any $x:\mathbf1\to X$, $y:X\to\mathbf1$, with arbitrary coupon networks defining $x,y$.

Rigidity gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i^*\otimes j)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i,j)$, zero unless $i=j$. When $i=j$ its generator is $b_i^R$, and $e_ib_i^R=d_i$ by sphericality. Hence $P_{i^*\otimes j}=\delta_{ij}b_i^Re_i/d_i$. Insert this into $R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})$. The right snake $(r_i\otimes1_i)(1_i\otimes b_i^R)=1_i$ retracts its first pair, and the left snake $(e_i\otimes1_{i^*})(1_{i^*}\otimes b_i)=1_{i^*}$ retracts the remaining pair. The resulting full morphism is $\delta_{ij}(D^2/d_i)1_{i\otimes i^*}$. Tensoring $g$ such disjoint pieces gives zero unless the entire color tuples agree and gives $D^{2g}/\prod_r d_{i_r}$ times the identity otherwise, with every multiplicity-space coupon retained.

For circumcision introduce a framed knot $K$ and a small zero-framed meridian $U$ meeting only $K$. In the finite $\Omega$ sum, $U$ acts on the simple $K$-color $j$ by $D^2\delta_{j0}$. The surviving coefficient is $d_0=1$, and the unit-colored knot, with all its framing and crossings, evaluates as the empty graph. Thus the full arbitrary-coupon exterior evaluation is multiplied by exactly $D^2$. If $K$ has framing $f$ and links the old surgery link by $\ell$, the new matrix is $B'=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}A&\ell&0\\\ell^t&f&1\\0&1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. Subtracting $\ell_z$ times the new meridian vector from each old vector gives $B'\cong A\oplus\left[\begin{smallmatrix}f&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. The last block has determinant$-1$ and signature0. Two new components contribute $D^{-2}$ and cancel $D^2$, with no signature or weight change. This proves the complete stated local identities, while leaving the genuine relative move-completeness theorem separate.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex modular spherical ribbon fusion category. Put $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, choose $D\ne0$, let $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, and $\Omega=\sum_i d_i i$. Write $b_X:\mathbf1\to X\otimes X^*$ and $e_X:X^*\otimes X\to\mathbf1$ for left duality, $r_X=e_{X^*}(j_X\otimes1)$ for right evaluation, and $b_X^R=(1\otimes j_X^{-1})b_{X^*}$ for right coevaluation. For $a:X\otimes Z\to Y\otimes Z$ define

$$\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)=(1_Y\otimes r_Z)(a\otimes1_{Z^*})(1_X\otimes b_Z),\qquad M_{X,Z}=c_{Z,X}c_{X,Z}.$$

Then $p_+p_-=D^2$, and the following are identities of complete morphisms, valid with arbitrary exterior tensor factors and coupons:

$$K_\pm(X):=\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i}^{\pm1})=p_\pm\theta_X^{\mp1}.$$

The zero-framed meridian operator $E_X=\sum_i d_i\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i})$ equals $D^2P_X$, where $P_X$ is the projection onto the full unit-isotypic summand. For $a\in\operatorname{End}(i^*\otimes j)$ define

$$R_{ij}(a)=(r_i\otimes1_j\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes a\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes1_{i^*}\otimes b_j).$$

The paired-handle/coupon contraction is

$$R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})=\delta_{ij}\frac{D^2}{d_i}1_{i\otimes i^*}.$$

Thus the normalized graph evaluation $D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F$ is unchanged under a signed generalized Fenn–Rourke twist-surgery move or circumcision adding a framed knot and its small zero-framed meridian. These are local algebraic identities; a complete presentation/move theorem is a separate topological assertion. No positivity, unitary conjugation, or anomaly cancellation is assumed.

A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category as in [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]], with finite simple-label set $I$, tensor unit $\mathbf1$, and dual label $i^*$ for each $i$. Define the **handle object**

$$H=\bigoplus_{i\in I}i\otimes i^*.$$

For an oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g$ with ordered marked points labeled by objects $W_1,\ldots,W_n$, fix a parametrization and the standard handle decomposition used to read its labels. The associated algebraic state space is

$$V(\Sigma;W_1,\ldots,W_n)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}\!\left(\mathbf1,\, W_1\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n\otimes H^{\otimes g}\right).$$

The empty tensor product is $\mathbf1$ and $H^{\otimes0}=\mathbf1$. Reversing the orientation of a marked boundary circle replaces its label $W$ by the left dual $W^*$. This formula defines a vector space only; mapping-class operators, bordism maps, independence of parametrization, and gluing are not asserted here.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex modular spherical ribbon fusion category. Put $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, choose $D\ne0$, let $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, and $\Omega=\sum_i d_i i$. For $a:X\otimes Z\to Y\otimes Z$ define

$$\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)=(1_Y\otimes r_Z)(a\otimes1_{Z^*})(1_X\otimes b_Z),\qquad M_{X,Z}=c_{Z,X}c_{X,Z}.$$

Then $p_+p_-=D^2$, and the following are identities of complete morphisms, valid with arbitrary exterior tensor factors and coupons:

$$K_\pm(X):=\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i}^{\pm1})=p_\pm\theta_X^{\mp1}.$$

The zero-framed meridian operator $E_X=\sum_i d_i\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i})$ equals $D^2P_X$, where $P_X$ is the projection onto the full unit-isotypic summand. For $a\in\operatorname{End}(i^*\otimes j)$ define

$$R_{ij}(a)=(r_i\otimes1_j\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes a\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes1_{i^*}\otimes b_j).$$

The paired-handle/coupon contraction is

$$R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})=\delta_{ij}\frac{D^2}{d_i}1_{i\otimes i^*}.$$

Thus the normalized graph evaluation $D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F$ is unchanged under a signed generalized Fenn–Rourke twist-surgery move or circumcision adding a framed knot and its small zero-framed meridian. These are local algebraic identities; a complete presentation/move theorem is a separate topological assertion. No positivity, unitary conjugation, or anomaly cancellation is assumed.

derivations.claim: Represent a standard cap by a ball containing one coupon and its marked strands, with one attached solid cylinder for each handle; the two bases of its handle arc are adjacent on the coupon. Reverse the coupon for the opposite raw cap. For a cylinder take two such disjoint standard handlebody neighborhoods in $S^3$ and, for each handle, a zero-framed surgery annulus surrounding its two opposed handle arcs. Choose mutually disjoint products $D_r\times[-1,1]$; inside each, the two handle arcs occupy small cylinders $B_r^-\times[-1,1]$, $B_r^+\times[-1,1]$ in an interior disk $D'_r\subset D_r$. Its surgery annulus is $D_r\setminus\operatorname{Int}D'_r$. Zero-framed surgery replaces its thickening by $D^2\times S^1$, attaching so that each $\partial D'_r\times\{t\}$ bounds a disk. That disk joined to the pair-of-pants $D'_r\setminus\operatorname{Int}(B_r^-\cup B_r^+)$ is an annulus between the two handle boundaries. As $t$ varies these are an annulus product, and the complementary portion of the filling solid torus leaves the ordinary cylinder between the punctured sphere boundaries. The product structures use the same $t$ coordinate on their collars, so they glue to $\Sigma_t\times I$ with its original parametrizations. This is a local coordinate proof of this particular cylinder presentation, not a completeness assertion. Its $g$ surgery annuli are zero-framed and mutually unlinked, so $m=g$, $\sigma(B)=0$.

Reading the oriented two opposed arcs in each disk product gives exactly $R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})$ of [F1]: the two bends are its specified $b_j,r_i$, and the surrounding annulus is its specified partial-trace meridian. Thus the complete graph word vanishes unless both handle tuples agree, and on $i=j$ it is $D^{2g}/d(i)$ times the identity of $X_{t,i}$. Arbitrary testing coupons give $F_{\rm cyl}(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{2g}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i$. Multiplying by the actual closed normalization $D^{-g-1}$ gives precisely $Q_t$. Its matrix in composition-dual bases is diagonal, with nonzero entries $D^{g-1}/d(i)$, so its inverse is the stated $N_t$. In particular its geometrically dual testing coupon to a raw basis vector $x_{i,a}$ is $D^{1-g}d(i)y^{i,a}$. This is a computation of the geometric Gram form, rather than confusing $\operatorname{tr}(1_{i\otimes i^*})=d_i^2$ with the cup/cap composition $r_ib_i=d_i$.

The raw pairing is perfect because a finite simple decomposition of $X$ has a unit-isotypic basis $x_a:\mathbf1\to X$, $y_a:X\to\mathbf1$ with $y_ax_b=\delta_{ab}$, and all nonunit summands contribute zero. Thus every capped multilinear functional defines a unique map $A_M$. Multiplying its outgoing block $j$ by $N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}=D^{\sum_q(1-g_q)}d(j)=D^{\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)$ gives the exact block formula in the Statement. Empty output has correction1. For disconnected bordisms the caps and all normalizations multiply, yielding the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi_{\rm out}/2$. The distinction between raw and geometrically dual cap coordinates is essential: one either inserts $N$ explicitly or absorbs it into the opposite cap basis.

In the cylinder formula the coefficient is $D^{-g-1+(1-g)}d(i)=D^{-2g}d(i)$, and the graph word is $D^{2g}/d(i)$ by step 2.1. Hence $Z_\alpha(\mathrm{cyl})=1$ on every color/multiplicity block. The outgoing empty-graph ball has $m=\sigma=0$ and $\chi_{\rm out}/2=1$, so its vector is1. The incoming ball has empty output and is multiplication by $D^{-1}$. Gluing them gives $D^{-1}=\tau(S^3)$, and the sphere cylinder has raw functional $D^{-1}yx$ corrected by $N_{S^2}=D$. Inserting an arbitrary handlebody coupon $x$ below the cylinder graph gives the decorated handlebody; the same local cancellation sends it to $x$. Thus every vector of the stated Hom space is realized. Tensoring gives the disconnected cylinder law. The empty bordism gives1, and disjoint union tensors the states, caps, $N$ factors and closed graph evaluations, proving its law.

For $r$ connected boundary tensor objects $X_q$ choose unit-channel composition-dual bases $x_{q,a},y_q^a$. Define $\iota(\bigotimes_qx_q)=\bigotimes_qx_q$ from $\bigotimes_q\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_q)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,\bigotimes_qX_q)$, and define $\pi(z)=\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_r}(\bigotimes_qx_{q,a_q})[(\bigotimes_qy_q^{a_q})z]$. Kronecker contraction gives $\pi\iota=1$, while $\iota\pi(z)=(P_{X_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes P_{X_r})z=D^{-2r}(E_{X_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes E_{X_r})z$. These maps are independent of the chosen unit bases because their object-level projectors are. For a special graph with disconnected input/output set $F_0=\pi_{\rm out}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,F)\iota_{\rm in}$ before the finite surgery-color sum. This retains precisely the required tensor-product channels; the larger Hom of the object tensor product is not silently identified with that tensor product of Hom spaces.

First suppose $M_1,M_2$ are connected and the common surface is connected of genus $G$. Stack their special graphs across a separating sphere. Each pair of matching open handle arcs joins to a surgery annulus, adding exactly $G$ components. A neighborhood of the separating sphere and the joined arcs is a sphere product with $2G$ one-handles; the disk/annulus surgery model of step 1.1 turns it into the product of the common genus-$G$ surface with an interval. Its complementary two pieces are the original bordisms with their cap parametrizations unchanged. Thus the stacked graph presents their glued bordism. If the middle color tuple is $j$, its new annulus weight is $d(j)$; categorical composition and the complete unit-channel resolutions therefore give $F_0(\Omega)^l_i=\sum_j d(j)F_0(\Omega_2)^l_jF_0(\Omega_1)^j_i$. This identity includes the sum over a full basis of every multiplicity Hom space, namely $\sum_ax_{j,a}y^{j,a}=P_{X_j}$ acting as the identity on its Hom from the unit.

Write $m_1,m_2$ for the old component counts and $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma$ for the actual old/stacked matrix signatures. Here $m=m_1+m_2+G$. The product of the two block coefficients of step 3.1 has $D$ exponent $-m_2-1+\chi_{\rm out}/2-m_1-1+(1-G)=-m_1-m_2-G-1+\chi_{\rm out}/2$, exactly that of the composite. Its remaining factors are exactly $d(l)d(j)$ as in step 5.1. The sole discrepancy is therefore $\kappa^{\sigma_1+\sigma_2-\sigma}$, proving the stated formula without assuming a Maslov theorem.

If the middle surface has $r\ge1$ components and total genus $G$, add $r-1$ zero-framed family-meridians at the separating sphere, each surrounding all arcs in one specified middle family. After the $G$ handle-annulus surgeries, the separating cylinder is the connected genus-$G$ surface product. Each family-meridian surgery compresses along its separating circle: remove $S^1\times I\times I$ and attach the two products $D^2\times I$ using the original collars. The $r-1$ disjoint compressions split it into exactly the $r$ prescribed middle surface products, so that graph presents the actual composite. If instead all $r$ family-meridians are added, the last one bounds a disk in one of those products and its surgery adds a separated $S^1\times S^2$ connected-sum factor. This proves the local graph-stacking model, including the previously missing disconnected families; it does not assert that all surgery diagrams of a bordism can be connected by these models.

Use the all-$r$ graph, with $m^+=m_1+m_2+G+r$. step 4.2 says its meridian sum inserts $D^{2r}$ times exactly the necessary $\iota\pi$ between the two exterior maps. Thus $F_0(\Omega^+)^l_i=D^{2r}\sum_jd(j)F_0(\Omega_2)^l_jF_0(\Omega_1)^j_i$. The closed connected-sum rule is $\tau(N\#P)=D\tau(N)\tau(P)$: place the two surgery links in disjoint balls; their component counts and signatures add, while the product normalization has one additional $D^{-1}$. The same argument holds for external cap graphs away from the sum balls. Since $\tau(S^1\times S^2)=1$, the extra factor is $D$ and must be divided out. The resulting $D$ exponent is $-m_1-m_2-G-r-2+\chi_{\rm out}/2+2r=-m_1-m_2-G+r-2+\chi_{\rm out}/2$. The product coefficients give exactly the same exponent because $\chi_{\rm middle}/2=r-G$. Every $d(j),d(l)$ also matches. The redundant final zero-framed trace component has signature0, so the actual signatures yield the same discrepancy $\kappa^{\sigma_1+\sigma_2-\sigma}$.

For disconnected $M_1,M_2$, decompose their bipartite component incidence graph, with edges the middle surface components. Isolated vertices simply tensor with the rest. In a connected incidence component with $a$ lower and $b$ upper vertices, connect-sum the lower pieces along $a-1$ pairs of interior balls and the upper pieces along $b-1$ pairs, avoiding all ribbon graphs. Their maps are multiplied by $D^{a-1}$ and $D^{b-1}$. In the already connected glued composite each such neck joins two balls in the same component, producing a connected sum with $S^1\times S^2$, and so multiplies its map by the same total $D^{a+b-2}$. The elementary neck is obtained by removing the two balls and joining their sphere boundaries by $S^2\times I$; it is the ordinary connected sum for balls in different components and the punctured $S^1\times S^2$ operation for balls in the same component. These added trace blocks have signature0. Apply the connected proof of step 6.1, step 7.1 and cancel the common nonzero $D$ power, proving the general composition formula componentwise. Together with step 4.1 this completes the cylinder, ball, tensor and empty laws and all normalized gluing scalars. A complete relative presentation theorem and the separate signature-to-Maslov comparison are still required before these fixed-presentation calculations are asserted as the full RT functor.
